title: Francis de Sales, patron of writers (24 January)
hookLine: when no one came to hear him, he slid pamphlets under doors

cards: A young priest stands in a village square in the hills south of Lake Geneva, ready to preach. Nobody comes. The town has become Reformed, Calvinist, and a Catholic preacher is not someone they want to hear.
Doors stay shut; some people won't even look at him in the street. He could leave, or shout louder. Instead he sits down at a table and writes short pages, clear and calm, one argument at a time.
Then, the story goes, he walks through town at night and slides them under the doors.

teach.h: SENT WHERE NO ONE WOULD LISTEN.
teach.b: Francis de Sales was a nobleman's son from Savoy who chose the priesthood over the career his father had planned.

His bishop sent him to the Chablais, the region around those shut doors, to win people back to the Catholic Church. Catholics and Reformed Christians remember that time from two sides, and both remember a struggle.
What Catholics remember about Francis is how he went about it: gently.
His leaflets, later gathered into a book, read like letters, not attacks. Over the years, people in that region did come back to the Catholic Church, and the Church credits his patience.
Later he became bishop of Geneva, though he lived across the border in Annecy, and he kept writing. His Introduction to the Devout Life was written for ordinary people, not monks.

A holy life, he said, looks different for a soldier, a shopkeeper, a married woman, a bishop; devotion should fit the life you actually have, the way a bee takes honey from a flower and leaves it whole.
With his friend Jane Frances de Chantal he also founded a community of sisters, the Visitation. The Church calls him a patron of writers. A Gospel line that fits him is Jesus in Matthew.
In the Douay-Rheims: "learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart".
Meek, in his hands, was not weak.

teach.h: LEARN OF ME, BECAUSE I AM MEEK.
teach.b: It was the patience to write one more page and slip it under one more door.

how: Catholics keep Saint Francis de Sales's memorial in January; writers and journalists honor him as their patron, and his Introduction to the Devout Life is still read by lay Catholics.

games.q: you're Francis, a young priest. you've come to preach, and nobody comes. doors stay shut. what do you do?
o: go home and ask to be sent elsewhere.
write short pages and slide them under the doors.
games.why: he wrote calm leaflets and slipped them under doors. they were later gathered into a book.

practice: Bring to mind someone whose door is a little shut to you right now, someone you've drifted from or disagreed with, and write them a few plain, kind sentences in your head: clear, unhurried, no argument, no pressure to reply.
If you pray, ask Francis de Sales to pray for the person who'd read it; if you don't, just hold their face in mind.

wordCard.voice: Francis. The bishop and writer Francis de Sales, who reached shut doors with gentle pages, and wrote that holiness should fit the life you actually have. A patron of writers.
